message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants you can find in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (and other branches) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and traditional Edomae style. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato Ward | Intimate setting, 3 Michelin stars; known for impeccable service and top‑grade fish. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Chuo Ward | 3 Michelin stars; focuses on seasonal ingredients and meticulous plating. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Chuo Ward | 2 Michelin stars; offers a refined tasting menu with a focus on freshness. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna and sashimi; long lines but worth it for the experience. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual chain; open 24/7; great value for a quick bite or late‑night craving. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic Edo‑style sushi; known for its high quality and elegant atmosphere. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Shinjuku | 1 Michelin star; small, intimate setting with a focus on seasonal fish. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Chuo Ward | 1 Michelin star; renowned for its omakase menu featuring rare cuts of fish. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Minato Ward | 1 Michelin star; offers a modern take on traditional sushi techniques. |

These restaurants range from high‑end, Michelin‑starred establishments to more casual yet still excellent spots. If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred venues. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
